about.title: Visalia Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Visalia sits at the crossroads of SR-198 and Rt 63, and much of the city's daily traffic funnels through S Mooney Boulevard and S Demaree Street. Public records for 2025 show 411 injury collisions inside city limits, leaving 558 people injured and eight traffic deaths. Those numbers describe a mid-sized Tulare County city of about 130,000 residents where a routine drive home can change in a moment, especially on Tuesday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when reported crashes cluster. If one of those collisions involved you, the days that follow can feel disorienting. Medical bills arrive before you are cleared to return to work, and the other driver's insurer may call sooner than you expect. We are a personal injury team that handles car accident claims on contingency. You pay nothing upfront, and we charge no fee unless your case produces a recovery. Our goal is to help you take the first step without financial burden.

items.title: Deadlines Are Explained Early
items.desc: California generally allows two years to file a car accident injury lawsuit, but a claim involving a city, county, or state vehicle or roadway can require notice in as little as six months. We can sort out which clock applies to your Visalia crash before it matters.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly responsible, with your recovery reduced by your share of blame. There is also no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost enjoyment of life in a standard car accident case.

items.title: Evidence Protected, Nothing Owed Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. We can also help you preserve photos, dashcam footage, and witness details while advising you not to give the other insurer a recorded statement.

items.question: My crash happened on SR-198 near the Mooney Boulevard exit. Does the location change anything?
items.answer: It can. Collisions on state highways are often documented by the CHP rather than Visalia police, so we will know where to request the report. If a government vehicle or a road-maintenance issue played any role, a shorter six-month notice deadline may apply. Getting in touch early keeps those options open.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is generally wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use casual remarks about how you feel or what you remember to reduce what they pay. Report the crash to your own insurer as your policy requires, and let us handle the rest.

items.question: I was texting at the light when I was rear-ended. Can I still make a claim in Visalia?
items.answer: Yes. California follows pure comparative fault, which means you can pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility. Your recovery would be reduced by whatever percentage of fault is assigned to you, but it is not eliminated. We can review the facts and explain how fault might be allocated in your situation.
